citation: Wadline startup radar. Each state is measured from public signals on the startup's own infrastructure; please cite the measurement date alongside the state.

signals.measures: days since the newest <lastmod> in the startup sitemap
days since the newest entry in the blog, changelog or release feed
days since the most recent push across the public repositories
days since the most recent published release
days since the normalised homepage last changed; requires two consecutive differing hashes, and strips scripts, nonces and build hashes

signals.role: gate: a failure forces the state to dormant regardless of the score
weighted zero: behind Cloudflare or Vercel the certificate rotates every 90 days regardless of whether the company still exists, so only an already-expired one carries meaning

method.normalisation: weights are renormalised over the signals that actually resolved, so a company with no public repository is not scored as though its repository were dead
method.unresolved: a signal with status 'unknown' (not measured) or 'blocked' (the site's robots.txt disallows us) carries no weight in either direction
method.minimum_evidence: no state and no score are published below 3 resolved signals, or with no time-based signal at all
method.reachability: a homepage that does not respond yields state=dormant and score=0 on its own, without needing the minimum above
method.closure: lifecycle_status is only ever set by a person. The measurement raises closure_candidate_at and a human confirms, because a failed request is as often a DNS migration or a bot block as a shutdown
method.collection: requests honour robots.txt, run one at a time per host with Crawl-delay respected, and identify as WadlineBot with a contact URL
method.not_measured: no vote counts, no traffic estimates, no social following. Nothing a submitter can influence by asking people to click
method.descriptive_fields: tagline, description, sector and logo describe the company rather than measure it. The first three come from the startup's own homepage metadata (og:site_name, the title, the meta description) and the sector is classified from that text against a fixed vocabulary; none of it is generated prose, and any of it may be null when a homepage publishes nothing usable
